subject: math.GR
name: Soficity of all groups
statement: Is every countable discrete group sofic, meaning it admits arbitrarily accurate finite permutation approximations that are asymptotically multiplicative and free on each prescribed finite subset?
importance: Would establish a common finite approximation principle behind major conjectures about group rings and dynamics.
status_note: Amenable, residually finite, and many other groups are known to be sofic; no general construction is known.

subject: math.GR
name: Residual finiteness of hyperbolic groups
statement: Is every word-hyperbolic group residually finite, so that each nonidentity element survives in some finite quotient?
importance: Would resolve how much finite algebra can detect the geometry of negatively curved groups.
status_note: Many hyperbolic groups are virtually special and hence residually finite; arbitrary word-hyperbolic groups are not covered.

subject: math.GR
name: Finitely presented infinite torsion group problem
statement: Does there exist an infinite finitely presented group in which every element has finite order?
importance: Asks whether finite defining data can support an infinite group consisting entirely of torsion.
status_note: Infinite finitely generated torsion groups are known; the finite-presentation requirement is the unresolved part.

subject: math.GR
name: Burnside problem at exponent five
statement: Is the free Burnside group B(2,5)=⟨x,y | w^5=1 for every word w in x,y⟩ finite?
importance: Represents a basic unresolved small-exponent case of a foundational finiteness problem.
status_note: Negative solutions for sufficiently large exponents and the solved restricted Burnside problem do not settle this particular free group.

subject: math.GR
name: Amenability of Thompson’s group F
statement: Is Thompson’s group F, consisting of dyadic piecewise-linear orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of [0,1] with slopes powers of two, amenable?
importance: Would clarify the boundary between finite-like averaging and nonamenable behavior in a fundamental transformation group.
status_note: F has no nonabelian free subgroup; this alone does not establish amenability, which remains open.

references.title: Groups with classifiable actions on the line

subject: math.GR
name: Andrews–Curtis conjecture
statement: Can every balanced finite presentation of the trivial group be changed to the standard trivial presentation by inverting a relator, multiplying one relator by another, conjugating a relator, and permuting relators?
importance: Links manipulation of finite presentations with deep questions in low-dimensional topology.
status_note: Many candidate counterexamples remain unresolved; the unrestricted classical conjecture has neither a proof nor an accepted counterexample.

subject: math.GR
name: Wiegold product-replacement conjecture
statement: For every finite nonabelian simple group G and k≥3, is the graph of generating k-tuples connected under elementary Nielsen moves replacing one entry by its product with another entry or its inverse, together with inversions and permutations?
importance: Would explain connectivity and reliability of finite-group generation procedures.
status_note: Verified for many families of finite simple groups; this is the finite-simple product-replacement conjecture, not Wiegold’s different normal-generation question.

references.title: Cohen and Vigdorovich, On the Maximal Size of Irredundant Generating Sets in Lie Groups and Algebraic Groups

subject: math.GR
name: Kaplansky zero-divisor conjecture for group algebras
statement: For every torsion-free group G and field k, is k[G] a ring without nonzero zero divisors?
importance: Would connect a purely group-theoretic torsion condition to a basic algebraic property of group rings.
status_note: Known for many group classes. Counterexamples to Kaplansky’s unit conjecture do not resolve this distinct question.

subject: math.GR
name: Gottschalk surjunctivity conjecture
statement: For every group G and finite alphabet A, is every injective continuous G-equivariant map A^G → A^G surjective, with the product topology and shift action?
importance: Asks whether finite local rules on a group obey a global injectivity-implies-surjectivity law.
status_note: Proved for sofic groups; the question for arbitrary groups remains open.

subject: math.GR
name: Kervaire normal-generation conjecture
statement: For every nontrivial group G, must the free product G * Z have normal rank at least two, so that no single element normally generates the entire free product?
importance: Asks whether adjoining one free generator can ever allow a single relation to collapse a nontrivial group completely.
status_note: The torsion-free case is proved, as are other important classes. The question for arbitrary nontrivial groups remains open.

references.title: Fisher and Lodha, A note on normal generation and the first ℓ²-Betti number
